summary: Retroactive hourly credit adjustments applied after regional failover causing invoice shortfall
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports retroactive hourly credit adjustments were applied to several running hours after an automated regional failover. The adjustments reduced billed usage lines for 2026-03-08 17:00-20:00 in us-west-2, producing a net negative line item that caused the customer's March invoice to under-report expected charges and created a negative pre-pay balance for their subaccount.

Impact:
- Greenline Health (enterprise) noticed a $9,120 shortfall on the March invoice relating to credits applied retroactively.
- Customer finance cannot reconcile month-end; accounting hold requested.
- No service outage; inference traffic unaffected.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: redwood-dedicated-usw2-gpu-a
- Region: us-west-2 (primary)
- Time window: 2026-03-08 17:00–20:00 UTC

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Scheduled leader election in us-west-2 triggered automated failover for the postback processing cluster at ~2026-03-08T17:13:04Z.
2) Postback consumer experienced transient connection errors; queue replay ran to backfill unprocessed messages.
3) Hourly credit reconciliation job (hourly-credit-aggregator) executed at 17:00 and again at 17:20 during the replay window, producing retroactive allocation entries.
4) Credits were associated with ledger entries that did not include invoice linkage metadata; downstream invoice render omitted the corresponding usage lines leading to a net negative balance on the invoice line for that hour.

Logs/attachments:
- Support console export: /attachments/SUP-872451/support_export_2026-03-08.zip
- Billing ledger snapshot: s3://redwood-billing-snapshots/2026-03-08/us-west-2/ledger.json
- Postback queue consumer logs (excerpt) included in comments.

Requested outcome by customer:
- Immediate reversal of the retroactive credit entries and a corrected invoice (or credit memo) to reflect actual billed usage.
- Root-cause explanation and assurance this will not recur.

investigation_notes: Initial analysis: postback queue replay during regional leader election caused the hourly-credit-aggregator to run twice for overlapping windows. The credit path lacked a stable idempotency token tied to original usage_postback_id, so the ledger accepted duplicates. Affected ledger entries were missing invoice linkage metadata because invoice-binding happens downstream and expected invoice_id was null for retroactive adjustments produced during replayed runs. Engineering replicated locally by replaying queue messages against a test ledger and confirmed duplicate entries appear when postback_id is not enforced. No evidence of tokenization or meter duplication in token counts — this is a billing allocation bug, not a metering overcount of usage.
resolution: Temporary fix: Manually reversed 12 retroactive allocations and issued credit memo CM-2026-03-1423 for $9,120; reissued corrected invoice. Permanent fix: merged PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4789 to enforce stable idempotency keys (usage_postback_id) in the credit allocation flow, added unit and integration tests, and updated the hourly-credit-aggregator to skip already-applied windows. Ops will deploy canary to staging and then prod. Follow-ups: runbook updated (confluence link), add alerting when hourly-aggregator run count > 1 in 30m window, postmortem scheduled.
